rss:physorg:7a5ebe3bfe54ff1549da9660.text: Gravitational lensing is one of astronomy's best tricks for seeing the early universe. When a massive galaxy cluster sits in between the observer and a distant object, its gravity bends and magnifies the distant object's light, acting like a giant natural magnifying glass. Galaxies that would otherwise be too faint to spot suddenly come into view because of gravitational lensing.

2611.09893.title: Challenges for minimal warm inflation in the Standard Model and beyond
2611.09893.text: A minimal realisation of warm inflation, even within the Standard Model, assumes that the inflaton $φ$ couples via the effective operator $φ\, G\tilde G$. We show that the SM solutions are in tension with the plasma calculation (as each sphaleron transition releases an energy much larger than the temperature) and with the assumed effective operator description. Embedding $φ$ as the Goldstone boson of a renormalizable Peccei-Quinn theory requires an anomaly coefficient $\gtrsim100$, implying a Landau pole for QCD. These tensions are relaxed for more strongly coupled dark gauge sectors.

2611.13951.text: Extended ionised gas tails can preserve a dynamical record of a galaxy's recent interaction with the intracluster medium (ICM). 2611.13881.text: Dust shapes the spectral energy distributions (SEDs) of stellar populations on every scale, from the circumstellar envelopes of evolved stars to the interstellar medium of galaxies. 2611.13583.text: Active learning is becoming standard practice in undergraduate STEM instruction in North America and is slowly being adopted in graduate courses. Graduate summer schools, one- to two-week programs in which students from many institutions gather for intensive, specialized instruction in their field, are common in physics; they are taught by researchers chosen for their expertise, and their pedagogy remains almost entirely traditional lecturing. 2611.13542.title: OASIS: A Fast Dynamical Halo Finding Algorithm
2611.13542.text: In recent work (García et al. 2023), we advocated for defining a dynamical halo as the collection of particles that orbit their self-generated potential. 2611.13519.text: Galactic supernova remnants (SNRs) interacting with molecular clouds (MCs) provide important laboratories for investigating how supernova feedback is transferred to the interstellar medium. 2611.13185.text: Giant radio galaxies (GRGs) are radio-loud active galactic nuclei (AGN) with projected linear sizes exceeding 0.7 Mpc, offering insights into the evolution of large-scale radio jets and their environments. 2611.13118.text: Astronomers often have difficulty determining whether an object, such as a star or galaxy of interest, has been discussed in the literature. 2611.13095.text: The nature of dark matter (DM) remains unknown, standing as one of the most pressing questions in modern physics. rss:physorg:177e09f8f4d3d16d550357c9.title: Independent technique validates landmark M87* image
rss:physorg:177e09f8f4d3d16d550357c9.text: The 2019 Event Horizon Telescope (EHT) image was the work of hundreds of scientists and captured the first direct view of a black hole's shadow—becoming one of the most recognized scientific images of the modern era. A team of four from CSIRO, Australia's national science agency, has developed a powerful new imaging technique that validated the landmark 2019 image of the black hole at the center of galaxy M87.

rss:universetoday:79cac5cdffe8e61d19fa90.title: The Ice Giants' Magnetic Fields are Very Strange Compared to Earth's
rss:universetoday:79cac5cdffe8e61d19fa90.text: Uranus and Neptune, the Solar System's ice giants, have interiors unlike the other planets. rss:physorg:fb2f81506dfbe2cae0d89580.text: Around 12 million light-years away, the supermassive black hole of the galaxy Centaurus A is hurling two enormous plasma jets into space at nearly the speed of light. These so-called jets are brighter at their edges than at their center. The reason for this was previously unclear but has now been explained by a team from the Chair of Astronomy at the University of Würzburg…

rss:universetoday:72b80c18b7c5b3680c751c.text: Science fiction authors have been dreaming of robotic spacecraft harvesting fortunes from asteroids for decades. rss:universetoday:eef1b2afb91b23370032c6.title: The Chandra X-Ray Observatory Unmasks a Supernova Impostor
rss:universetoday:eef1b2afb91b23370032c6.text: Some stars, called Luminous Blue Variables, can be confused with supernovae explosions. They exhibit similar outbursts, but unlike supernovae, which explode once and then are gone forever, these stars have periodic outbursts. New research found that one of these 'supernova impostors' is in a binary relationship with a black hole or a neutron star, and that explains its periodic outbursts.
